READING
THE LIMIT IS THE FEATURES, NOT THE MODEL. No learned arm clears its own permutation band:
set transformer 0.539 vs 95th 0.572 (p=0.100)
Eight statistics off a rigid-body scan do not contain which of ten enzymes is the catalyst,
and neither a weighted combination nor attention across the group conjures it. Capacity was
never the bottleneck here -- the representation is. A bigger head on the same features is
not the next move; a different measurement is.
DOES THE MID-PACK RULE SURVIVE A DIFFERENT DECOY DRAW? (run 1 of the pilot, same 60
reactions, decoys drawn on a different criterion -- an independent sample of decoys)
draw                                midpack AUC    true-catalyst z sd
this run (atom-matched)                   0.633                 0.731
run 1 (length-matched)                    0.491                 1.021
A random member of a z-scored set of 10 has sd ~1.0.
IT DOES NOT SURVIVE. On the other draw the rule is worth 0.491 and the true
catalyst's z has sd 1.021 -- indistinguishable from a random member. So the
mid-pack regularity is a property of WHICH DECOYS WERE SAMPLED, not of catalysts, and
the network's apparent margin is fitted to one draw. It would not transfer.
For contrast, where a network DID earn its margin in this project: GeoConv reached 0.617 on
interface point pairs against a 0.566 best single feature -- but that task is scored on a
complex that already exists. The model was not the difference; having the true interface was.
